purpose: Migration fidelity fixture. These are the answers a resuming run got from the LEGACY records at 193f408, before the canonical system replaced them. tools/resume_check.mjs re-derives the same answers from the canonical records and fails on any difference. Without this, the resumption check would only prove the new records are self-consistent, not that they resume to the same place the old ones did.

expected.objective_statement: Continue CINDERLINE from the published Gate B representative-slice checkpoint and implement the highest-priority verified frontier without overstating full Gate B coverage.
expected.active_task_title: Add save migration and regression tests
expected.next_action: Implement GB-H1 as an isolated save-migration layer, then verify old-version fixtures, staged migrations, explicit failure recovery, current saves and normal save/load behavior before integration.

state_revision.reason: The migration is itself a state change and bumps the revision.

last_verified_checkpoint.reason: The migration created a new checkpoint. Its verified_action restates the previous one verbatim so nothing is lost.

rollback_point.reason: The legacy value was stale. Two later commits had already modified the very records that named it, so rolling back there would have discarded decision OD-005, failure OF-006 and the publication evidence. See ledger event MIG-20260801-05-BASELINE-RECONCILED.

derived_frontier.reason: GB-IMP02 and GC-IMP06-FULLRUN already satisfied the eligibility rule and were simply not listed; the legacy validator only checked listed entries, never completeness. Selection order is unchanged — GB-H1 is still the active task. See ledger event MIG-20260801-06-FRONTIER-CORRECTED.

working_branch.reason: The actual checkout. The legacy value did not match reality.

objective_id.reason: The legacy record had no identifier for the objective, only its text. The text is unchanged and is what the fidelity check compares.
